mainTopic: Testing רב אסי's rule that money in the תורה means Tyrian silver, rewording it to cover fixed amounts only, and a new source for בית שמאי's דינר minimum for קידושין.
overview: Earlier on the דף, רב אסי taught that whenever the תורה says כסף (money), it means a full silver coin, a כסף צורי. The גמרא first tests this rule with three cases: the oath over a claim, מעשר שני, and הקדש. Each time it answers that the case has a special source of its own: a comparison to 'vessels', the extra word 'the' in the פסוק, or a גזירה שוה from מעשר. A fourth challenge comes from קידושין. There בית הלל allow just a פרוטה, so רב אסי would seem to agree only with בית שמאי. The גמרא therefore rewords רב אסי's rule: only a fixed amount in the תורה is Tyrian money, while amounts set by the חכמים are cheaper local money. The new point turns out to be the rabbinic half: the חכמים' fine of a סלע for striking someone is only half a זוז. Then ריש לקיש offers a different source for בית שמאי's דינר minimum, from חזקיה's teaching that an אמה עבריה can deduct from her redemption price. The גמרא pushes back on that proof, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the oath over a claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that every כסף in the תורה means a full silver coin. In the case of a claim about a deposit, the פסוק says כסף, yet the משנה sets the minimum claim at only two silver מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a claim? It is written: 'If a man gives his neighbor money or vessels to guard.' And we learned in a משנה: the judges' oath applies when the claim is at least two silver coins and the admission is at least a פרוטה's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a case that seems to break the rule that 'money' in the תורה always means a full silver coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about deposits uses the word כסף. If that meant a full silver coin, the minimum claim should be a large amount. But the משנה says only two small silver מעה are needed, so the rule seems to fail here.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim, here a demand in court that someone owes money or a deposit
The oath imposed by the judges, here on someone who admits to part of a claim
Admission, the defendant agreeing that he owes part of the claim
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin value that counts in הלכה
'But there is…', a standard way the גמרא brings a case that contradicts a rule

phrases.english: But there is the case of a claim, as it is written:
"If a man gives to his neighbor
money or vessels to guard"
And we learned in a משנה: the oath of the judges applies when
the claim is two silver coins,
phrases.notes: These are two small silver מעה, much less than a full silver coin, and that's exactly what causes the problem.

phrases.english: and the admission is worth a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of challenges, from earlier on the דף, against the rule that every כסף in the תורה is כסף צורי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that every mention of כסף in the תורה means a full silver coin (כסף צורי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about deposits says כסף, yet the משנה sets the minimum claim at just two small silver מעה, not a full coin.

steps.title: Money is compared to vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the deposit פסוק, 'money' is learned from its neighbor word 'vessels'. Just as 'vessels' means at least two, 'money' means two coins. And just as money is valuable, the vessels must be valuable too.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, money is read like vessels. Just as 'vessels' means two, 'money' also means two. And just as money is something significant, the vessels must also be something significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the deposit case has its own special source, so it does not break the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the minimum amount comes from comparing 'money' to 'vessels' in the same פסוק. The plural 'vessels' teaches 'two', so 'money' also means two coins, of any small size. This special comparison overrides the general rule only in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other case
Similar to, read in the same way as
'Just as… so too…', the form of a comparison
A significant item, something of real value

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the source for two rules: the minimum claim of two מעה, and the rule that the oath applies only to items of value.

phrases.english: There, money is similar to vessels:
just as 'vessels' means two,
so too 'money' means two coins.
And just as money is a significant item,
so too the vessels must be a significant item.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Special source: a comparison within the same פסוק explains why this case is different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק says כסף, the minimum claim should be a full silver coin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because 'money' sits next to 'vessels', it means two coins of any size. The general rule still stands for other cases.

steps.title: Challenge from second tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another challenge. The פסוק about מעשר שני says 'the money', yet a משנה shows that מעשר שני can be held in copper coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about מעשר? It is written: 'And bind up the money in your hand.' And we learned in a משנה about someone who breaks a סלע from coins of מעשר שני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second case where 'money' in the תורה does not seem to mean a silver coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about redeeming מעשר שני says כסף. But the משנה talks about trading מעשר שני copper coins for a silver סלע. That shows copper coins can count as מעשר שני money, which goes against the rule of silver only.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
'And you shall bind up', wrapping the money to bring it to ירושלים
Breaks or exchanges a large coin for smaller ones, or the reverse
A large silver coin

phrases.english: But there is the case of tithe, as it is written:
"And bind up the money in your hand"
And we learned in a משנה: one who exchanges for a סלע
from coins of second tithe!
phrases.notes: He holds copper coins as מעשר שני money and trades them for a silver סלע. So copper works too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the same general rule, after the first challenge was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that every כסף in the תורה means a silver coin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעשר פסוק says כסף, yet copper coins are allowed for מעשר שני.

steps.title: The extra word 'the' includes other coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says 'the money' (הכסף), not just 'money' (כסף). The extra letter ה widens the meaning to include any coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'the money' instead of 'money', and that adds to the meaning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the מעשר פסוק has an extra word that makes it an exception to the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word כסף would mean a silver coin. Because the פסוק adds 'the' (הכסף), the extra letter is read as including more, such as copper coins. So מעשר שני is a special exception, and the general rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It included, meaning an extra word widens the law

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'the' here is not just grammar. The גמרא treats the extra ה as a deliberate hint that widens the law.

phrases.english: Instead of "money" it says "the money", and that includes more.
phrases.notes: The extra ה ('the') is read as adding other coins, like copper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מעשר שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual inclusion: an extra word in the פסוק widens the law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר שני money would have to be silver, since the פסוק says כסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק says הכסף, any coin, including copper, is allowed for מעשר שני.

steps.title: Challenge from redeeming הקדש for a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a third challenge. The פסוק about redeeming הקדש says כסף, yet שמואל rules that הקדש worth a מנה, redeemed for something worth only a פרוטה, is validly redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about הקדש? It is written: 'And he shall give the money and it will be his.' And שמואל said: הקדש worth a מנה that was redeemed for something worth a פרוטה is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third case where 'money' in the תורה seems not to mean a silver coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הקדש פסוק uses the word כסף. Yet שמואל allows redemption with as little as a פרוטה, a tiny copper value. That seems to go against the rule that כסף means a full silver coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
A large sum, one hundred דינרים
He redeemed it, moving its holiness onto something else
It is redeemed, the redemption works

phrases.english: But there is the case of consecrated property, as it is written:
"And he shall give the money and it will be his"
And שמואל said: consecrated property worth a מנה
that one redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the same general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that every כסף in the תורה means a full silver coin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הקדש פסוק says כסף, yet שמואל lets הקדש be redeemed for just a פרוטה's worth.

steps.title: הקדש learns from מעשר through a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הקדש learns from מעשר through a גזירה שוה on the shared word כסף. Since any coin is allowed for מעשר, any coin is allowed for הקדש too.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, he learns 'money' from 'money' in the case of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that הקדש is also a special exception, because it borrows its rule from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כסף appears in both the הקדש פסוק and the מעשר פסוק, which links them through a גזירה שוה. מעשר was already widened by the word הכסף, so הקדש is widened too. The general rule of a silver coin stays in place for all other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
He learns, derives
Learning one law from another through a shared word in both פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: These three challenges are answered the same way. Each case has its own special source: 'vessels', 'the money', or a גזירה שוה from מעשר. The rule survives these cases, but the next challenge, from קידושין, forces the גמרא to reword רב אסי's rule (step 8).

phrases.english: There too, "money" and "money":
phrases.notes: The same word appears in both places, and that links the two laws.

phrases.english: he learns it from tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הקדש challenge by building on the answer about מעשר in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה: a shared word passes the מעשר exception on to הקדש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הקדש would need a full silver coin to be redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש follows מעשר through the shared word כסף, so even a פרוטה's worth can redeem it.

steps.title: Betrothing a woman with a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: קידושין is learned from a פסוק about money, yet בית הלל allow it with a פרוטה. Does רב אסי only agree with בית שמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about betrothing a woman? It is written 'When a man takes a woman,' and we learn 'taking' from 'taking' in the field of עפרון, which was bought with money. Yet the משנה says בית הלל allow it with a פרוטה or something worth a פרוטה. Shall we say רב אסי holds like בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth challenge to רב אסי's rule that 'money' in the תורה always means high-value Tyrian coins. It uses קידושין, which works with money but needs only a פרוטה according to בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money in קידושין comes from a גזירה שוה with עפרון's field, so it counts as 'money of the תורה.' If רב אסי were right, קידושין would need a big Tyrian coin, which is the view of בית שמאי. But the הלכה follows בית הלל, who need only a פרוטה, so רב אסי's rule seems to go against the accepted view.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothing a woman
'Taking.' This is the shared word that links קידושין to the purchase of עפרון's field
The field אברהם bought from עפרון with money
The smallest coin of value
The students of שמאי. Here they require a large sum (a דינר) for קידושין

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge about the coin in עפרון's field. The point is that the 'money' of קידושין is learned from the תורה, yet בית הלל allow a tiny amount for it.

phrases.english: But there is the betrothal of a woman,
as it is written: "When a man takes a woman and lives with her,"
and we learn "taking" from "taking" in the field of עפרון,
phrases.notes: אברהם 'took' עפרון's field by paying money, so 'taking' a wife can also be done with money.

phrases.english: and we learned in the משנה: בית הלל say:
with a פרוטה or with something worth a פרוטה.
Shall we say that רב אסי
stated his rule like בית שמאי?!
phrases.notes: In the first משנה of the מסכת, בית שמאי require a full דינר for קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the הקדש challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a fourth and stronger case against רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that all 'money' in the תורה is כסף צורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קידושין money is learned from the תורה, yet the accepted view of בית הלל allows just a פרוטה. So רב אסי would match only the rejected view of בית שמאי.

steps.title: Restating רב אסי: fixed תורה amounts versus rabbinic amounts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reworks רב אסי's statement. Only a set, fixed amount in the תורה is כסף צורי, while amounts set by the חכמים are כסף מדינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this. רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: every fixed sum of money stated in the תורה is Tyrian money, and every sum set by the חכמים is local money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the old version of רב אסי's rule and replaces it with a narrower one. Now it covers only fixed sums written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new key word is קָצוּב, meaning fixed or set. קידושין has no fixed sum in the תורה, so it is not covered, and בית הלל's פרוטה is no problem. The new version also adds a second half: sums set by the חכמים are measured in the cheaper local coin.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it was said, this is how it was said.' A formula for rewording an earlier statement
A fixed, set amount of money
Tyrian money, the heavy, high-value coinage
Local (provincial) money, worth much less
Set by the words of the חכמים, meaning rabbinic

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי's final rule: a fixed amount in the תורה is כסף צורי, and a rabbinic amount is כסף מדינה.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
this is how it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב אסי said:
Every fixed amount of money stated in the תורה
is Tyrian money,
and an amount set by the חכמים is local money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the קידושין challenge by narrowing רב אסי's rule instead of defending the original version.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every mention of 'money' in the תורה means Tyrian coinage.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fixed sums in the תורה are Tyrian. Rabbinic sums are local coinage, and קידושין, which has no fixed sum, is not included.

steps.title: Isn't this already taught in a משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב אסי adds, since a משנה already lists the תורה's fixed payments in Tyrian coinage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: five סלעים for a firstborn son, thirty for a slave, fifty from a rapist and a seducer, and a hundred from one who spreads a bad name. All of them are paid in the holy shekel, in Tyrian coinage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version of רב אסי's rule as unnecessary. A משנה already says that the תורה's fixed payments are made in Tyrian coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists exactly the fixed sums the תורה names and says they are all in שקל הקודש, the Tyrian standard. So the first half of רב אסי's rule seems to repeat what we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he teaching us?' This asks what new point a statement adds
סלעים, coins each worth four זוזים in Tyrian money
A man who forces, or a man who seduces, an unmarried girl. Each pays fifty
A husband who falsely accuses his bride. He pays a hundred
The holy shekel, the Tyrian standard of coinage

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
five סלעים for redeeming a firstborn son,
thirty for a slave,
phrases.notes: This is what an ox's owner pays when his ox kills a slave.

phrases.english: fifty from a rapist and from a seducer,
a hundred from one who spreads a bad name,
all of them are in the holy shekel,
in Tyrian coinage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the new version of רב אסי's rule as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first half of the reworded rule: fixed תורה amounts are כסף צורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already states this explicitly for every fixed תורה payment, so the rule would be redundant.

steps.title: The new point is the rabbinic half: a fine of a 'סלע' is local money
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי's חידוש is the rabbinic half. For example, the חכמים' fine of a סלע for striking someone means the local coin, worth half a זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: The part 'a rabbinic amount is local money' was needed, because we did not learn it. As a ברייתא teaches: one who strikes his fellow gives him a סלע. Do not say a סלע here means four זוזים. Rather, it means half a זוז, because people commonly call half a זוז an 'איסתירא' (a סלע).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second half of רב אסי's rule is the new teaching. It shows a rabbinic fine that is measured in the cheap local coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in בכורות covers only the תורה's fixed amounts and says nothing about amounts set by the חכמים. So רב אסי teaches that a rabbinic 'סלע' fine is the small local coin people call איסתירא, worth half a זוז, not the Tyrian סלע worth four זוזים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needed to say it.' This shows a teaching is not redundant
One who strikes or blasts his fellow to shame him
A זוז, the same as a דינר
Half a זוז
The everyday name for a סלע. Locally it meant a coin worth half a זוז

steps.whatToRemember: When the חכמים set a fine in 'סלעים,' it means the cheap local coin, not the Tyrian סלע of the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets how much is actually paid for rabbinic fines, like the fine for shaming someone. It is far less than the תורה's sums.

phrases.english: "And an amount set by the חכמים is local money"
was needed for him to say, since we did not learn it.
As a ברייתא teaches: one who strikes his fellow
gives him a סלע.
phrases.notes: This fine was set by the חכמים, so it is a rabbinic amount.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא תֵּימָא מַאי סֶלַע – אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי,
phrases.english: And do not say: what is a סלע? Four זוזים.
Rather, what is a סלע? Half a זוז,
since people commonly
call half a זוז an איסתירא.
phrases.notes: איסתירא is the everyday name for a סלע, so in local speech a 'סלע' was this small coin.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְשֶׁל דִּבְרֵיהֶם כֶּסֶף מְדִינָה״ אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, דְּלָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the 'what does he teach us' challenge by showing the rabbinic half is new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the non-redundant part of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי's rule just repeats the משנה in בכורות.
steps.terutzMaskana: His new point is that rabbinic sums, like the סלע fine for striking someone, are paid in local coinage worth half a זוז.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: בית שמאי's reason comes from חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says בית שמאי's דינר minimum is based on חזקיה, who learns from 'והפדה' that an אמה עבריה can deduct from her redemption price and go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: The reason of בית שמאי is like חזקיה. חזקיה said: The פסוק says 'והפדה,' which teaches that she subtracts from her redemption price and goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new explanation, from ריש לקיש, for why בית שמאי require a דינר for קידושין. He sets up a teaching of חזקיה that the next step will use as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה reads 'והפדה' as saying an אמה עבריה can buy her freedom early by paying her price minus the part she already worked off. The assumption is that בית שמאי compare regular קידושין to buying an אמה עבריה. The next step explains how this leads to a דינר minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל
An early אמורא whose teaching ריש לקיש relies on
'Then he shall let her be redeemed,' the פסוק about an אמה עבריה
She subtracts from her redemption price, paying only for the time left
A Jewish maidservant, bought for a set amount of money

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
The reason of Beit Shammai is like Chizkiyah.
For Chizkiyah said: The verse says: "Then he shall let her be redeemed"
This teaches that she subtracts from her redemption price, and goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, כִּדְחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב אסי's explanation and gives a separate source for בית שמאי's דינר rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי's דינר minimum rests on חזקיה's reading of 'והפדה': an אמה עבריה deducts from her redemption price.

steps.title: Why deducting requires a price bigger than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: Deducting makes sense if she was bought for a דינר, since she can go down step by step to a פרוטה. You cannot deduct from just a פרוטה, so the purchase price must be at least a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say he gave her a דינר: then she keeps subtracting down to a פרוטה. But if you say he gave her a פרוטה, can she subtract from a פרוטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how חזקיה's teaching proves בית שמאי's view. Deducting needs room to go down, and a פרוטה has no room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרוטה is the smallest amount of money, so a price of one פרוטה cannot be reduced. Since the תורה says she can deduct, she must have been bought for more, at least a דינר. Comparing קידושין to an אמה עבריה, קידושין would also need a דינר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works well if you say...', which shows one option fits
A silver coin worth many פרוטות
The smallest coin that counts as money
'Can she subtract?', a question meaning she obviously can't

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a law about a maidservant ends up setting the minimum amount for קידושין in בית שמאי's view.

steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's rule that the minimum is a דינר
steps.raayaSupportSource: חזקיה's reading of 'והפדה': deducting is only possible if the price is more than a פרוטה.

steps.title: Maybe a פרוטה purchase simply has no deducting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the תורה means that if he paid a דינר she deducts down to a פרוטה, but if he paid a פרוטה there is no deducting at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying: Where he gave her a דינר, she subtracts down to a פרוטה. Where he gave her a פרוטה, she does not subtract at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's proof. The deducting rule might only apply when the price was big enough, and it does not show that a פרוטה purchase is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that deducting must always be possible, so the price must always be big. The גמרא says the deducting rule can be read as applying only to bigger purchases. So a פרוטה purchase could still be valid, just without the option to deduct, which puts the source for a דינר minimum in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But perhaps', which opens another way of reading that weakens a proof
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה, ה׳
She does not deduct at all

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא challenges the proof for בית שמאי from חזקיה. Deducting might apply only to a דינר purchase, while a פרוטה purchase would still work but have no deducting. The discussion of this challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does NOT say a פרוטה purchase is invalid. It says the opposite is possible: the purchase works, and only the deducting option is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 12 by offering another way to read חזקיה's deducting rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof in step 12 that the purchase price must be at least a דינר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed deducting must be possible in every purchase. The deducting rule may apply only when a דינר was paid, so a פרוטה purchase could still be valid.
